correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructs all quantifiers and cases using random uniform priorities, negative within-union covariance, positive continuous maxima covariance and law of total covariance. A symbolic exact algebra reduction was zero; 707 independent exact rational checks from a standalone verifier cover all size/overlap parameters through seven primary species plus complete two-network distributions. Finite tests do not establish universal claim; analytical proof does.

originality.rationale: Inspected full primary publications from 2004, 2012, 2018 and 2024. The 2024 degree-only expected-robustness formula and the 2018 empirical distributions of robustness are prior results, not new. No inspected source supplied the signed joint last-neighbor rank covariance or the exact same-degree fourfold variance separation. Closest theoretical coverage gives first moments, not second moments; historical equivalence in probability theory remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: A previously published equivalent overlapping-subset order-statistic covariance formula could exist under classical probability terminology, beyond the primary material inspected.
A linked supplementary appendix of the 2024 article was not separately retrieved; main text explicitly presents second-moment uncertainty as future work.
Extensions to weighted interactions, cascades or nonuniform extinction ordering are not proved.

value.rationale: Network robustness variance is a meaningful exact uncertainty metric under random ecological extinctions, especially because Jones et al. (2024) already show mean robustness depends only on degrees. New overlap-sensitive covariance has a sharp sign threshold, and a degree-matched pair of eight-vertex 2-regular graphs has variance ratio exactly four, separating uncertainty from expected robustness. This is not a marginal special case or unmotivated table value.
